newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Soccer-Moshoeu inspires South Africa to second win.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Moshoeu inspires South Africa to second win.

text.p: John Moshoeu turned on a superb individual performance to inspire South Africa to a 2-0 win over 10-man Australia in the Four Nations Cup in Johannesburg on Wednesday.
Moshoeu scored the opening goal and ran a relentless midfield attack against an Australian team who were down to 10 men after Tony Popovic was sent off in the 27th minute.
The result puts South Africa at the top of the standings in the week-long tournament with maximum points from their first two matches.
Australia share second place with Ghana who beat Kenya 1-0. Both have three points from two games.

Turkey-based Moshoeu, who flew into the country just one day before the match, gave the home team the perfect start with a tap-in goal after 13 minutes after Mark Williams had carved through the Australian defence.
Williams added the second in the 71st minute for his first goal for South Africa since scoring both in the country's 2-0 triumph over Tunisia in February's African Nations' Cup final.
It was a finely taken individual effort with Williams turning his marker inside the penalty area before slotting the ball past Australian goalkeeper Zeljko Kalac.
South Africa were always on top of the Socceroos who lost Popovic when he picked up a second yellow card for dissent after earlier being booked for a deliberate handball.
South Africa now need just a draw in their final match against Ghana in Pretoria on Saturday to retain the annual trophy.
Earlier, Ghana and Kenya plodded through 90 minutes of uninspiring football with substitute Nana Dartey scoring the winner just four minutes from the end.
Ghana missed a succession of chances against their game opponents before Dartey, playing only his second full international, headed home from a corner.
Ghana must now beat South Africa in the final match on Saturday to have any chance of winning the tournament. Earlier, Australia meet Kenya in Pretoria.
